cases.label: approved_style
reasoningMoves: Identify what context was already provided
Identify the missing callable interface/usage knowledge
Compare direct remedy with indirect or overbroad alternatives
cases.prompt: An AI coding agent was asked to implement a user lookup API. It already received the repository folder tree, snake_case naming rule, API endpoint specification, and example response. Yet it reimplemented its own database query and date conversion rather than reusing existing functionality. The real project contains database.connection and utils.py with usable functions. The passing endpoint test replaces both helpers with one-argument stubs. The usage example for the installed helpers comes from an import job in the same revision. Its two calls use a connection and a date policy prepared in a separate startup file. An API request trace shows that middleware passes the handler an open connection of the same type and the same date policy. Which handoff supplies enough evidence to call both helpers correctly with the least extra code to read?

options.text: Provide the two calls from the passing endpoint test, require reuse, and check the generated diff for duplicate logic.
Provide the real interfaces and usage examples of the relevant existing modules and explicitly require their reuse.
Provide the installed helper interfaces, the import job’s two calls and its startup file, and require reuse of both helpers.
Require a longer implementation plan and self-review before code generation.

cases.rationale: A and D can help but do not teach the agent the callable existing API. C also provides the installed interfaces and usage examples, but adds startup-file code that is unnecessary for this API request because middleware already supplies the connection and date policy. B supplies targeted project-specific context and gives the model a concrete reuse path.

distractorReasons.A: Post-generation detection, not relevant missing interface knowledge.
distractorReasons.C: C supplies enough information to use the installed helpers, but adds startup-file code that need not be read because middleware already provides the connection and date policy.
distractorReasons.D: D asks for a self-review without specifying how to check the planned calls against the installed helper interfaces. The passing endpoint test exercises stubs, so that test alone cannot establish that the calls match.

hints: Separate the observations in the scenario from assumptions about what the agent knows. Which facts were explicitly supplied before implementation?
Compare each proposed intervention by what information it changes at implementation time, and the trade-offs it introduces.
For each option, check whether it supports a correct implementation and whether it adds avoidable context or merely shifts the work to a later check. Then choose the most justified approach.
cases.scenarioProvenance: Synthetic developer scenario applying Ch.1 context-bundle principles; mention actual utils.py as scenario information, not a verbatim chapter fact.

cases.label: approved_style
reasoningMoves: Diagnose why actual project facts are unavailable
Assign different roles to plan/status/meeting evidence
Handle conflicts by date and authority without blind overwrites
Distinguish instruction format from access to domain data
cases.prompt: A team asks an AI to summarize project progress, remaining risks and next week's priorities. The model currently receives only a plan written three months ago. Material A is that plan (goals and intended scope). Material B is the latest task/status ledger (completed, ongoing and unresolved bugs). Material C is recent meeting decisions (changed deadlines and priorities). In 6-10 sentences, explain (1) why the AI report is inaccurate, (2) how to use A/B/C and reconcile conflicts, (3) why simply writing a longer prompt cannot solve the problem.
cases.modelAnswer: A three-month-old plan establishes intent, not the present state. Material A identifies original goals and intended scope. Material B can supply observed completed or ongoing work and unresolved issues; an unresolved bug does not by itself prove the entire workstream is blocked. Material C records decisions about deadlines and priorities. For each disputed field, compare the document's date, purpose and responsible source, and explicitly mark what remains unknown. Request the missing evidence before asserting a current state or obstacle. Create a focused bundle of goals, verified status, decisions and uncertainties, then format the report. A longer instruction alone cannot supply missing current facts.
hints: What can the AI know from an old plan, and what kinds of facts about today cannot be inferred from that plan?
Separate the three materials by their roles: intended goals, observed progress, and decisions about future work. What if they conflict?

Draft a checking sequence: first label what is known from each document; next identify conflicts or unanswered factual questions; finally decide what extra verification is needed before writing a current-status conclusion. Keep the conclusion in your own words.
rubricCriteria: Explains context deficit rather than treating poor wording as the sole cause
Explains timestamp/authority-sensitive conflicts without blind overwrite
Contrasts better instructions with real project knowledge

cases.label: rejected_low_quality
cases.prompt: What book orientation is directly supported by the cover subtitle 'practical AI service guide'?
cases.reason: Cover-only bibliographic recognition; no technical learning; implausible distractors; could be solved without studying chapter 1.

cases.label: rejected_low_quality
cases.prompt: How should ISBN 979-11-7579-005-6 be treated in a study note?
cases.reason: Publisher/ISBN fact; irrelevant to AI/Agent learning objective; must not auto-fallback to front-matter quiz.

cases.label: rejected_too_easy
cases.prompt: A chatbot forgets the previous message because it was not passed to the model. Which fix is best: (A) be friendlier (B) pass previous messages (C) add generic shipping knowledge (D) self-review?
cases.reason: Question reveals missing information and answer almost verbatim; one-step recall with trivial alternatives, not 2-3 step reasoning.

cases.label: rejected_redundancy
cases.prompt: Five questions each rephrase 'Can we infer technical details solely from cover/title?' and two case analyses ask the same limitation.
cases.reason: Superficially different stems test the same knowledge and reasoning operation; not acceptable concept coverage.

cases.label: rejected_display
cases.prompt: Answer appears 'A\n정답: \"A\"'; source shows 'excerptId=; PDF pageIndex=1' and literal '**구절 식별자**'.
cases.reason: Leaky internal annotations, duplicated answer line and missing/garbled citation binding.
